summary: In-process parallel tagging for the 4B finetune: one tag_concepts.py run saturates the server's slots, replacing manual chunk-id sharding across processes

analysis.author: Hermes Agent
analysis.content:
Goal (owner, 2026-08-15): saturate the 4B finetune's server slots from a single tag_concepts.py invocation, so a bulk pass needs no external orchestration -- no agent fanning out, no hand-sharded chunk-id files, no N terminals.

VERIFIED STATE OF THE CODE (read before planning, not assumed):

  scripts/serve-llama.sh already exposes --parallel, defaulting to 1, and
  scripts/run-qwen-4b-guru.sh already sets PARALLEL=4. So the SERVER side of
  this is done: the 4B is served today with 4 concurrent slots. Its header
  states the intended usage explicitly -- "lets multiple tag_concepts.py
  instances run in parallel against disjoint --tradition / --text scopes" --
  which is exactly the external orchestration this ticket removes.

  scripts/tag_concepts.py run_tagging() is a strictly serial
  `for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks)` loop over one sqlite connection:
  resolve chunk path -> read TOML body -> build_prompt -> call_llm (blocking,
  seconds) -> parse_tags -> upsert_staged_tag -> mark_complete. The LLM call
  is the only slow step; everything else is local file/DB work in
  milliseconds. So the concurrency that matters is exclusively around
  call_llm.

  run_tagging already sets PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000, and its comment names
  the reason: "WAL allows concurrent readers but one writer; parallel worker
  runs (--chunk-ids-from-file shards) need a wait instead of an instant
  'database is locked' crash." That is the existing multi-process story. A
  single-process worker pool can do better than tolerating write contention:
  keep every DB write on one thread and the contention disappears rather than
  being waited out.

  scripts/llm.py call_llamacpp() is stateless -- per-call urllib request, no
  shared client object -- so it is safe to call from multiple threads as-is.
  One catch for the multi-endpoint work below: it resolves the server address
  from os.environ["LLAMACPP_BASE_URL"] at call time, which is process-global.
  Targeting two servers therefore needs the base URL threaded through as a
  parameter; a thread-local env hack would work but would be a trap for the
  next reader.

  serve-llama.sh takes --host/--port/--n-gpu-layers/--parallel and no device
  flag, so GPU selection is environmental (CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=..., per docs/ingest/gpu-assembly.md, which also
  records that this rig's un-pinned CUDA order is inverted relative to
  physical device 0).

SHAPE OF THE FIX. Producer/worker/writer inside one process: the main thread
feeds chunks to a bounded ThreadPoolExecutor whose workers do only the pure
part (read body, build prompt, call_llm, parse), and results come back to a
single writer that owns the connection and does upsert_staged_tag +
mark_complete. Serial behaviour is the N=1 case of the same code path, so the
existing accounting, --resume semantics and outcome counters survive intact.

HARDWARE ENVELOPE. The 4B is Q4_K_M at ~2.5 GB against a 24 GB 3090, so slots
are limited by KV cache and context, not weights -- 4 is a conservative
starting point rather than a ceiling, and the honest way to raise it is to
measure. The 4070 (12 GB) can host a second server on another port for
roughly double throughput, which is what the multi-endpoint child is for.
Both are subject to the standing rules: announce GPU use, `llm stop` when
done, and comfyui cannot share the 3090.

SCOPE GUARD. Parallelism is opt-in and belongs to the finetune. The 27B
teacher is served with think-on as the standing default and occupies far more
VRAM; multiplexing it is not in scope and the flag should not silently invite
it.

VALIDATION. The last child re-tags mesopotamian.enuma-elish (12 chunks)
through the new path. That is both the smoke test for the framework and the
live test of the todo:32e9d1de taxonomy-drift hypothesis: v3's training
snapshot contains concept.cosmogony, the text has never had it proposed in
any status, so if the drift theory is right this run proposes it. If it does
not, the theory is wrong and we learn that for the price of 12 chunks instead
of a 2,342-chunk backfill.
